title: 6 'spookiest places' in Lancs - including hotel 'haunted' by heartbroken ghost
excerpt: From 'haunted' castles to chilling moorland, Lancashire is brimming with spooky tales and ghostly legends.
content:
From 'haunted' castles to chilling moorland, Lancashire is brimming with spooky tales and ghostly legends.

Visit Lancashire has named six of the county’s most haunted sites, each with its own eerie history and supernatural sightings.

Pendle Hill, infamous for the 17th-century Pendle witch trials, is among those mentioned and spooky happenings are also said to have taken place at Lancaster Castle is alongside a hotel in Accrington

Here are six of Lancashire's most 'haunted' locations:

Pendle Hill is said to be haunted by the restless spirits of accused witches and has made the list.

The Visit Lancashire website said: "Lancashire’s long and rich history is part of the county’s lasting appeal, however as with every good historic tale, it usually comes with something a little more sinister.

"Explore the hill by yourself or take part in one of the many walking tours available."

Ten of the 12 Pendle witches were hanged after being found guilty of witchcraft and murder, and visitors to the hill have reported sensing their presence.

Lancaster Castle, another site with a grim past, was used during the witch trials and later served as a prison.

Spooky sightings include shadowy figures, floating orbs, sudden low temperatures and the sounds of crying.

Public hangings were once carried out at the castle, adding to its chilling atmosphere.

Further south, Samlesbury Hall is said to be one of the most haunted houses in England.

Linked to tales of murder, suicide, and execution, the hall is thought to be home to numerous spirits.

Among them is the ‘White Lady’, believed to be Dorothy Southworth, who is said to have died of a broken heart and is often spotted crossing the nearby road.

Ghost tours are available throughout the year or why not stay at the hall and see if you can spot a spectre.

Hoghton Tower is so famously haunted that staff keep a dedicated ‘ghost file’ to document paranormal events.

The most frequently sighted apparition is the ‘Green Lady’, described as wearing green velvet and often seen laughing softly.

Other reported spirits include a monk, a little girl, and even a phantom black dog.

The 19th-century Winter Gardens theatre in Morecambe is said to be haunted by several ghosts, including a former seamstress who longed to perform on stage.

Visitors and performers have reported shadowy figures, unexplained noises, and even being pushed or slapped.

A spokesperson said: "Ghosts reported include a little girl, a monk and a black dog, but most commonly seen is the Green Lady, who is dressed in beautiful green velvet and appears to be chuckling to herself."

The Mercure Dunkenhalgh Hotel & Spa in Clayton-le-Moors, a 700-year-old manor turned hotel, is reportedly haunted by the ghost of Lucette, a former governess.

Her tragic story tells of heartbreak after being deceived by an army officer, leading her to take her own life by jumping from a bridge.

Lucette is said to be most active during the festive season, particularly on Christmas Eve, when guests claim to see her wandering the hotel wrapped in a winding sheet.

Have you ever experienced the paranormal in Lancashire? Leave your stories in the comments below.
